newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bilbao Vizcaya puts up $328 mln for Banco Ganadero.
newsitem.headline: Bilbao Vizcaya puts up $328 mln for Banco Ganadero.

text.p: Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya completed its purchase of a 40 percent stake in Colombia's Banco Ganadero by snapping up more than 1.25 billion ordinary shares, bank officials said.

They said the deal was valued at $328 million and Bilbao Vizcaya now had equal representation on Ganadero's new board of directors, which was elected at an extraordinary shareholders meeting immediately after the share buyout.
Miguel Largacha, Ganadero's general-secretary, said the board would be chaired by Jesus Villamizar of Ganadero. But the bank's new executive president is Jose Ayala of Bilbao Vizcaya.

Largacha said Bilbao Vizcaya had purchased 425.62 million already issued ordinary shares through a public offer, at a previously agreed price of 295 pesos per share. It then purchased an additional 831.52 million new ordinary shares at 260 pesos per share.
At the shareholders meeting, Ganadero's by-laws were amended to ensure its legal existence until December 31, 2099.

Completion of the sale was hailed by one government official as an unquestionable sign of international confidence in Colombia's economy, despite the political uncertainty dogging it for the past year.
"It's a light of hope, not just for the stock exchange, but for the whole economy," he said.

Ganadero is Colombia's No. 1 bank in terms of assets, according a report issued earlier this week from the country's Banking Superintendency. The report said those assets, as of June 30, 1996, stood at 3.27 trillion pesos, a 30 percent increase from the close of the first half in 1995.
